title: WHO ETAT Pediatric Triage (Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment)

triggers.description: Capillary refill > 3 s with cold hands and weak fast pulse → EMERGENCY

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Triage of all sick children on arrival: assign EMERGENCY (immediate treatment), PRIORITY (front of queue), or QUEUE (routine). Check emergency signs first — treatment starts before full assessment.

sections.heading: Emergency signs (ABCD) — treat immediately
steps: Airway/Breathing: obstructed breathing, central cyanosis, or severe respiratory distress.
Circulation: cold hands with capillary refill longer than 3 seconds and weak, fast pulse.
Coma / Convulsions: unconscious child or currently convulsing.
Dehydration (severe): lethargy, sunken eyes, very slow skin pinch return — in a child with diarrhoea.

sections.heading: Priority signs — front of the queue
steps: Tiny baby: any sick infant under 2 months.
Temperature: child is very hot (high fever).
Trauma or other urgent surgical condition.

sections.heading: No emergency or priority signs
paragraphs: QUEUE: assess and treat in order of arrival.
